The CHitResult payload is 62 bytes: a 22-byte header (qword tag 0x32 performer at +0x18, u16 tag 0x12 at +0x20, u16 tag 0x12 at +0x22, u32 tag 0x14 at +0x24, u8 tag 0x0B at +0x28) whose four non-identity fields are PINNED AT ZERO, a 3-byte u16 count of 1, and one 37-byte hit entry (qword tag 0x32 target at +0x00, u32 tag 0x14 at +0x08 READ SIGNED, three tag-0x2A floats at +0x0C, tag-0x2A yaw at +0x18, u16 tag 0x12 flag word at +0x1C), giving an 84-byte PC and a 95-byte frame for every step. The four steps are HIT_WEAK (damage -63, flags 0x0001), HIT_STRONG (damage -379, flags 0x0001), MISS (damage 0, flags 0x0000) and HIT_REACTION (damage -63, flags 0x0009), labelled HYP_PF_024_DAMAGE_MODEL_<STEP> and spaced 0.0 / 6.0 / 6.0 / 6.0 s on the frozen V141 sender's cumulative deadline. THE NUMBERS ARE OURS. Round 83 (DAMAGE-MODEL-001) proved byte-exactly that the client computes nothing: no damage formula, no scaling, no subtraction from hit points, and the figure a player sees is the signed i32 at hit-entry +0x08 passed through abs() and printed with a plain integer format, so there is no original formula in the image to recover and the owner approved designing one (2026-08-19 11:45, scope: one signed i32 plus one flag word per target). The formula is integer-only and deterministic with no RNG: ATK = 100 + 7*(str+bonus_str) + 3*level, DEF = 10 + 2*(con+bonus_con) + 1*level, base = max(ATK-DEF, 1), damage_wire = -base, computed with unbounded Python ints and range-checked at the end rather than wrapped, masked or clamped. The defender is the character as the HYP-PF-020 sweep leaves it (level 7, con 22 -> DEF 61) so a tester can check the arithmetic off the character sheet; MOB_WEAK (str 3, level 1 -> ATK 124) gives 63 and MOB_STRONG (str 40, level 20 -> ATK 440) gives 379, both deliberately not round and not squares. THE SIGN IS THE MEANING: +0x08 is compared signed at four cmp/jge sites, negative is the took-damage side, and the player still sees a positive number because the display path calls abs(); a positive value is refused outright because heal/absorb/no-op semantics are UNKNOWN, and INT32_MIN is refused separately because abs() built from cdq/xor/sub returns 0x80000000 unchanged and would print a minus sign on the one path designed never to show one. The flag word is an allowlist of whole values {0x0000, 0x0001, 0x0009} with a second mask check against 0x0009 and a forbidden mask of 0xF184; bit 0 is chosen deliberately rather than left zero because 0x7509DA gates the whole reaction block on it while the number is drawn by a second pass that does not read it, and bit 4 is refused on every frame of this sweep because it makes the client play _F_KNOCKED_002 INSTEAD of showing the figure. The MISS frame is the experiment's control and validate_damage_model_sweep refuses any sweep without one. The performer and the target are BOTH the player's own actor, a design choice and not a claim about how a real hit looks: it is the only identity this lane can be sure the client knows, and an entry whose TARGET cannot be found is skipped at 0x7508AD / 0x750D27 while a missing PERFORMER is not (0x7507C3, 74 25). The position is the frozen hash-pinned V135 player spawn and the yaw is pinned at 0.0f because it is an angle fed to sin/cos, not a magnitude. THE LANE IS ONE-SHOT: a repeat trigger returns [] with damage_model_hypothesis_already_sent_no_reply, because the value of the two hit numbers is that a tester can predict them before they appear. Everything fails closed with no bytes and no write: a non-int or bool damage, a positive damage, INT32_MIN, a value below the -1,000,000 safe band or outside the -9999 scenario band, a flag word that is not u16 or carries a forbidden or out-of-mask or out-of-allowlist value, a zero paired with the reaction bit or a non-zero without it, the number-suppressing bit, a non-pinned yaw or a non-float32 one, a position that is not the pinned source, an identity outside the qword range, an entry count other than 1, a non-zero reserved header field, a forged or missing unlock token, a scenario object or file outside the exact allowlist, a step index outside the plan (including True and -1), a formula input outside the declared u16 domain, a formula output that does not reproduce, composed bytes that do not match the pin, and a sweep with no MISS frame.
